_comment: Shard definitions for test projects too large to run as a single unit.
A package listed here has its test suite split into shards; a package that
is not listed runs as one unit. Shards are crossed with the tier filters
(deterministic / coyote / chaos) by plan-test-matrix.py, so a shard is a
slice of a project's tests and a tier is a slice of a shard.
ORDERED FIRST-MATCH-WINS. Shards are evaluated top to bottom and a test
belongs to the FIRST shard whose include prefixes match it. The generated
filter for shard i is therefore OR(its own includes) AND NOT(includes of
every earlier shard). This is what makes the list a PARTITION rather than
an allow-list: every test lands in exactly one shard, so a suite cannot
silently lose coverage to a gap between two patterns, and two shards
cannot both claim the same test and run it twice.
The ordering is load-bearing. 'BPlusTree.ChaosPredicate' must precede
'BPlusTree.Chaos', which must precede 'BPlusTree.', because each is a
prefix of the one before it. Put a broad prefix above a narrow one and the
narrow shard silently runs nothing - which is why the leg summary reports
the executed test count per shard and the aggregate report flags any shard
that ran zero tests in every tier.
The final shard must set "complement": true. It matches everything no
earlier shard claimed, so adding a new test namespace can never fall
outside the partition and go untested.
Prefixes are relative to namespaceRoot and are matched against the VSTest
FullyQualifiedName, which is Namespace.Class.Method. A trailing dot pins
the match to a namespace segment ('Grains.'); no trailing dot lets it
match a class-name prefix ('ChaosPredicate'), which is how the chaos
fixtures that all share one namespace are split.
CROSSING WITH TIERS IS OPTIONAL. By default a sharded package's shards are
crossed with the deterministic / coyote / chaos filters, so each shard
becomes three invocations. That pays off only when the tiers are
independently large enough to fill separate runners, which is true of
'lattice' and of nothing else so far. A package whose suite carries no
Chaos and no Coyote category at all sets "crossTiers": false and gets one
untiered invocation per shard instead, saving two empty process starts per
shard. It is safe against a future fixture because it removes the tier
filter rather than naming the tiers to keep: the shard expressions are
still a partition, so a new Chaos test lands in a shard and runs.

shards.note: 7 predicate fault-injection fixtures.
The remaining Chaos*IntegrationTests fixtures.
Per-grain unit tests. Largest by file count, cheap per test; the split-link leaf/root regression slice ran 17 tests in 0.791s locally, so it remains in this shard.
Persistent state POCO tests.
339 reflection-driven contract assertions, 66s of the BPlusTree root's 245s. Split out because it was the single largest contributor to the critical path leg.
Topology, restart, durability and Coyote fixtures in the BPlusTree root.
CRDT and low-level primitive unit tests.
Smaller cross-cutting areas grouped into one shard.

The TLC mutation gates are CPU-bound JVM runs, so they are split across their own shards by the TlcShard* category test/lattice/Formal/TlcCiShard.cs gives each case (a category, because the NUnit adapter's filter parser rejects a FullName prefix that ends inside a case's argument list). Sizes are test-minutes summed over the cases of CI run 37322771720, which the harness runs about four at a time, so wall-clock is about a quarter. This shard holds every Replication EventualConvergence (temporal) mutant: they share one control arm, which the harness runs once per process, about 54 test-minutes (15 minutes wall-clock in that run).

The mutants of the replication companion modules (ReplicationReBootstrap, ReplicationLowWatermark, ReplicationCausalDelivery) and ReplicationLowWatermark's variant configurations, about 66 test-minutes, 60 of them ReplicationReBootstrap's. Each module's mutants share their controls, so every companion module stays whole in this shard.
The other Replication mutants plus the mutants of every Wal* module, about 55 test-minutes (14 minutes wall-clock in that run).
The mutants of every ShardOwnership* module, about 62 test-minutes (16 minutes wall-clock in that run).

The mutants of every AtomicCommit* module, kept whole because mutants of one module share their control arms. Variant configurations are balanced across six formal-tlc-atomic-variants-* shards because they have no shared control arms.
State-weighted AtomicCommit* variant group 1 of 6. Variants are assigned by deterministic longest-processing-time balancing over manifest distinctStates.

The mutants of every Backup* module, about 30 test-minutes.
One retained base-model TLC smoke check on every routine CI run. Exhaustive base models and mutation gates remain in the full formal-tlc shard.

Every other TLC case: the base run of every module, variant runs of every module but AtomicCommit*, mutations of ungrouped modules (including BPlusTopology), and synthetic-module gates. BPlusTopology's 15 base/mutation cases took 13s locally, too small to justify a dedicated runner; the catch-all historically measured about 35 test-minutes. Before the AtomicCommit*, Backup* and ReplicationReBootstrap groups were split out it was 165 test-minutes, 42 minutes of wall-clock.
Root-namespace fixtures plus PublicApiContract, Hygiene, Fakes, Docs, Testing.
3.3 min over 198 tests. Store, memory-convergence and TTL fixtures; the heaviest area per test by a wide margin.

1.9 min over 991 tests. Host integration plus the two reconciler areas that pair with it.
2.2 min over 1166 tests. Root-namespace fixtures plus Archive, Bootstrap, Claims, Content, Docs, Fakes, Graph, Harness, Source, Usage.
